Dr Harry Coleman
General Practitioner
St Kilda Health Clinic 
35 Carlisle Street 
St Kilda, 3182

13/09/2008

Dear Dr Coleman,

Re: Mr Joel Silbersher, aged 12

I am writing to refer Joel who was admitted to our hospital on 10 September due to diabetic ketoacidosis. He is now ready to be discharged and requires a follow-up at your service. 

Upon admission, Joel presented with symptoms of dehydration, orthostatic hypotension, tachycardia, acetone breath, fatigue and weakness along with GI problems. Given to his medical history of type 1 diabetes, he was diagnosed as diabetic ketoacidosis.

During hospitalization, Joel has been treated with IV fluids, intravenous insulin therapy, and electrolyte and potassium replacements. His blood sugar has also been monitored regularly. As a result, his condition has gradually improved, and glucose was added to his IV fluids after his blood sugar being stabilized. He has also been placed on a diabetic diet.

Joel and his family have been taught about the prevention of a diabetic ketoacidosis recurrence, as well as the importance of carrying his medical ID and letting his closed ones know the action to hypoglycemia. Please follow up on his compliance with medications as well as his management of diet and exercise. 

If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact me. 

Yours sincerely,

Yu Hisn, Liu
RN(188 W)
